cues: Chapter one, what maladaptive daydreaming actually is, how
it is measured, and who has it.
Here is the plain definition.
Maladaptive daydreaming, or MD for short, is compulsive,
vivid, story -like fantasy.
It is often launched on purpose, with music
and movement.
The person craves it, struggles to stop it,
and lets it crowd out real life, work,
relationships, and sleep.
The idea has a short history.
In 2002, Illy Summer names it after treating
six patients.
In 2011, a survey of 90 people calls
it compulsive fantasy.
In 2016 comes the first scale, tested in
45 countries.
In 2017, researchers propose formal criteria.
And in 2025, 27 experts asked for it
to be listed as a dissociative disorder.
Summer, a psychologist in Israel, defined it as
extensive fantasy activity that replaces human interaction or
interferes with study, relationships, or work.
He believed it grew from a normal childhood
talent for imagination, which hard circumstances turned into
a problem.
In 2011, Bigelsohn and Shupak surveyed 90 self
-identified fantasizers and proposed the name compulsive fantasy.
79 % moved their bodies while fantasizing.
The distress came from losing control of the
urge, from fantasy getting in the way of
real relationships and goals, and from intense shame.
They estimated that fantasy filled about 56 %
of their waking hours.

quizzes.full: Slowed and reverb. It is sad-leaning and nostalgic, and sad music increases inward, emotional mind-wandering.

quizzes.q: A recall from chapter five. What are the two ways background sound breaks your thinking?
quizzes.a: Changing sound breaks order; understandable words compete with meaning
quizzes.full: Changing sound disrupts holding things in order, and understandable words compete with meaning. Rap hits both.

quizzes.q: Which two techniques top the evidence ranking, and which popular ones sit at the bottom?
quizzes.a: Top: self-testing and spacing. Bottom: rereading, highlighting, summarising.
quizzes.full: Testing yourself and spacing your practice are at the top. Rereading, highlighting and summarising are at the bottom.

quizzes.q: In the GPT-4 study, what happened once the AI was taken away, and what fixed it?
quizzes.a: 17% worse without it. Hint-only tutoring largely fixed it.
quizzes.full: Students scored 17 percent worse than those who never had it. A tutor that gave hints instead of answers largely removed the harm.

quizzes.q: A recall from chapter six. What did repeatedly watching how-to videos do to people's confidence, and to their skill?
quizzes.a: Confidence up, skill unchanged. A hands-on attempt breaks the illusion.
quizzes.full: Confidence went up. Actual skill did not. Only a brief hands-on attempt reduced the illusion.

quizzes.q: Your skills are profession-like. If not raw hours, what are your levers?
quizzes.a: Feedback loops and mental models (pattern libraries)
quizzes.full: Better feedback loops and better mental models: pattern libraries built by labelling examples and practising from them.

quizzes.q: What should you ask a mentor, instead of what's your advice?
quizzes.a: ‘Walk me through the last time you did this.’
quizzes.full: Walk me through the last time you did this. Experts leave out about 70 percent of their decisions when they explain.

quizzes.q: A recall from chapter seven. Is YouTube packaging a kind or a wicked learning environment, and what does that mean for practice?
quizzes.a: Semi-wicked: noisy, delayed feedback. Volume, prediction logs, tests.
quizzes.full: Semi-wicked. Feedback is noisy and delayed, so gut feel is unreliable. Use high volume, prediction logs and tests.

quizzes.q: What is the rule for using AI when your goal is learning?
quizzes.a: Attempt first, then AI critiques and explains
quizzes.full: Attempt first, then use AI to critique and explain. Hints, not answers.

quizzes.q: Name three of the five features that separate incubation from escapism.
quizzes.a: Loaded problem · bounded activity · capture · return · process, not success
quizzes.full: A loaded problem first, a bounded low-demand activity, capture, a return to the work the same day, and imagining process and obstacles instead of success.

quizzes.q: A recall from chapter eight. What is the risk of a scheduled ideation slot for someone with MD?
quizzes.a: It can become a gateway into immersion: cap it, write it, track it
quizzes.full: It can become a sanctioned gateway into immersion. So cap it, write rather than just imagine, and track your total fantasy time.

quizzes.q: What is the one approach the MD trial showed does not work?
quizzes.a: Willpower + forums. Mindfulness + daily self-monitoring worked.
quizzes.full: Willpower plus online forums. The wait-list group did not improve. Mindfulness plus daily self-monitoring did.

quizzes.q: Build the plan part of a WOOP for your music urge.
quizzes.a: If I reach for earbuds during work, then I put them away, breathe, and do one 2-minute step in silence.
quizzes.full: For example: if I reach for my earbuds during work, then I put them in the other room, breathe, and do one two-minute step in silence.

quizzes.q: What three markers define maladaptive daydreaming?
quizzes.a: Immersion · compulsion · cost
quizzes.full: Immersion, compulsion and cost.

quizzes.q: Which technique beat cramming with an effect of 0.74?
quizzes.a: Spaced retrieval: testing yourself at intervals
quizzes.full: Spaced retrieval: testing yourself at intervals.

quizzes.q: What makes music a problem for you, beyond distraction?
quizzes.a: It drives imagination: 2.7× more vivid, deeper, harder to exit
quizzes.full: It drives imagination: scenes 2.7 times more vivid, deeper immersion, and harder exits. For 36 of 41 people with MD, music deepened the daydream.

quizzes.q: In the loop, what comes right after instant relief?
quizzes.a: The habit strengthens
quizzes.full: The habit strengthens, so the urge comes faster next time.

quizzes.q: Over 13 months, what did MD predict, and what did not predict MD?
quizzes.a: MD → later stress, anxiety, depression. Not the reverse.
quizzes.full: MD predicted later stress, anxiety and depression. Distress did not predict later MD.

quizzes.q: Why ask a mentor to walk you through the last time, instead of asking for advice?
quizzes.a: Experts omit ~70% of their decisions when explaining
quizzes.full: Because experts leave out about 70 percent of their decisions when they explain how they work.

quizzes.q: What are the four parts of WOOP, and which kind of obstacle do you name?
quizzes.a: Wish · Outcome · Obstacle (inner) · Plan
quizzes.full: Wish, outcome, obstacle, plan. And you name the inner obstacle.
